title: RotateClientSecret
description: The body of an administrative secret rotation, derived from identity_application::applications::RotateClientSecret. The grace period is the field that makes this a rotation rather than an outage, and its absence is the field that makes it one anyway.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; RotateClientCommand has no body and no route serves it

actor_id.description: The administrator rotating it. Required for the same reason as on registration: a command that changes a credential and does not name an actor has no way to be authorized.

application_id.description: The application whose secret rotates. An internal identifier, not the client_id: this is an administrative surface addressing a row.

grace_period_ms.description: Keep the previous secret valid for a grace period, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Some(0) means INVALID IMMEDIATELY — that is the emergency case, and the field being an Option<i64> rather than a bool is what makes "expire it now" expressible as a value rather than as a different endpoint. Absent means the implementation's own default, which this contract does not state because no code states it yet.
grace_period_ms.x-serde-note: Option<i64> with no skip_serializing_if, so the key is always present on the wire.
grace_period_ms.x-why-a-grace-period: Rotation with a grace period is the difference between a rotation and an outage: a client that has not yet picked up the new secret keeps working while operators roll it out. Without the previous_secret_valid_until_ms in the response, a caller could not tell a rotation with a grace period from one that cut everyone off at once.

x-response: RotateClientSecretOutcome — { client_secret: string, previous_secret_valid_until_ms: integer }. The new secret is shown once, on the same terms as at registration.

x-refusals.public-client: ApplicationError::Domain — a public client has no secret to rotate. This is a refusal rather than a no-op returning null, because a rotation that quietly did nothing is indistinguishable at the call site from one that worked.

x-phase: Phase 4 — OIDC provider (client registration and the confidential/public distinction)
